prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1090; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the insured's representative regarding a side impact collision at a controlled intersection involving the insured vehicle and a second vehicle. The claimant reports a knee injury and has retained counsel.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy record and confirmed the driver involved is listed as a named driver and coverage was in force at the time of loss.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant's attorney, who confirmed representation and asked that all future contact go through their office. The account of the collision was provided in writing and matches the initial report.

Entry 4: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the time of impact and records the collision as described. The responding officer noted the points of impact on both vehicles.

Entry 5: Interviewed two independent witnesses at the scene, who each confirmed the collision happened as the claimant described and that the claimant was seated in the driver's vehicle.

Entry 6: Reviewed scene and vehicle photographs. The damage pattern on the claimant's vehicle lines up with the side impact described, and the damage on the other vehicle is consistent with the same event.

Entry 7: Took a recorded statement from the other driver, who independently confirmed the sequence of events and the signal status at the intersection.

Entry 8: Checked prior claim and damage history for the vehicle and found no earlier damage recorded to the same areas. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 9: Received medical records showing treatment for a knee injury. The injury is the kind expected from this type of force, and no prior injury to the same knee appears in the records reviewed.

Entry 10: Treatment followed a typical course, with therapy and follow-up visits tapering as the claimant's condition improved and the treating provider noted steady progress.

Entry 11: Reviewed the claimant's statements from each contact so far. The account of the collision and the injury has stayed the same across every conversation and in the written submission.

Entry 12: Current assessment: liability and coverage are consistent with the documentation, the injury and vehicle damage fit the described impact, and the file is being prepared for continued handling through counsel.
